claims.text: Punjab Police deployed over 2,000 personnel at Lovely Professional University after student protests over an alleged rape turned violent.
ADGP M F Farooqui stated that police personnel would remain deployed on the LPU campus through the night to maintain security.
Protesting students pelted stones at police personnel and attacked police vehicles outside LPU on Sunday evening.
Protesting LPU students blocked National Highway 44 outside the university starting around 8 am on Sunday.
Police used a lathi charge to attempt to clear protesting students blocking National Highway 44.
Two police vehicles were set on fire during the LPU campus protests.
Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh stated that reports of disturbances inside LPU hostels were rumours and checks found no such incidents.
Lovely Professional University postponed its mid-term examinations and suspended regular classes for 10 days starting September 28.
Student protests at Lovely Professional University in northern India erupted following social media claims that a female student was raped at a girls' hostel by a worker.
Lovely Professional University denied the allegations of rape on campus, describing them as rumours.
LPU Registrar Dr. Monika Gulati released a video featuring three female students residing in Room 504 of Girls' Hostel 3 who denied that any assault took place in their room.
A subsequent video emerged showing the three female students from Room 504 stating that LPU administration instructed them on what to say and posted their video without consent.
Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk stated that four to five police vehicles were damaged in the violence.
DIG Naveen Singla stated police registered a case based on statements that a female student was sexually assaulted around three days prior and returned home.
During Sunday evening protests at LPU, academic buildings were torched and explosions were heard from inside the campus.
DIG Naveen Singla stated that protesting students raised concerns regarding a student from Telangana who died by suicide on the LPU campus a fortnight prior.
Punjab Police registered an FIR containing rape charges against unknown persons and constituted a special investigation team to probe allegations.
Protesting LPU students demanded that university founder-chancellor and Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Mittal personally come to the protest site to assure action.
Protests erupted a day earlier at Chitkara University in Patiala over social media rumours alleging two female students died by suicide.
Bank unions called off a proposed three-day nationwide strike after the Indian Banks Association agreed to form a high-level committee to deliberate on declaring remaining Saturdays as holidays.
State-run bank branches operated on Sunday following government orders to ensure bank customers were not inconvenienced ahead of the planned strike.
The United Forum of Bank Unions deferred its planned nationwide strike from September 28–30 following a meeting with the Indian Banks' Association at 9:30 pm on Sunday, September 27.
The Reserve Bank of India approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches, and currency chests on Sunday, September 27.
Indian bank branches are currently closed on the second and fourth Saturdays of every month while other Saturdays remain working days.
The IBA and UFBU agreed to begin discussions on modifying the Performance Linked Incentive scheme for officers in Scale IV and above.
AIBEA General Secretary C. H. Venkatachalam stated that all banks will function normally and there will be no strike.
An online meeting lasting about one hour was held between seven bank union representatives and six banking executives on Sunday night.
Devidas Tuljapurkar, chairperson of All India Bank of Maharashtra Employees' Federation, expressed satisfaction over the decision to form a committee regarding a five-day work week.
The proposed three-day bank strike was scheduled to begin on Monday and coincide with the half-yearly closing period for banks.
A political row erupted after a video surfaced showing Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma allegedly slapping a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar.
AAP MLA Jarnail Singh attended the road inspection in Tilak Nagar and questioned the quality of the road after pulling out sections of its surface by hand.
Saheb Singh, who handles social media for AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, alleged that Parvesh Verma snatched his phone, hit him, and security personnel grabbed him by the neck.
Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma claimed AAP workers hurled abuses at his family during the inspection and alleged MLA Jarnail Singh sought a commission from PWD engineers.
Delhi AAP chief Saurabh Bharadwaj was detained by police during a protest in Tilak Nagar over the incident.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the BJP government of using force against people who question authority following the slap incident in Tilak Nagar.
Former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal demanded the arrest of Minister Parvesh Verma and announced plans to inspect the Tilak Nagar road.
Delhi BJP media head Praveen Shankar Kapoor claimed Saheb Singh is a habitual offender previously arrested for allegedly assaulting an MCD employee.
Parvesh Verma was seen slapping a man in Delhi.
Scroll.in reported Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma as holding the position of Delhi Deputy Chief Minister.
Saheb Singh stated that he and AAP MLA Jarnail Singh went to the Tilak Nagar site after being called by the Public Works Department to inspect the road.
Saheb Singh submitted a formal complaint against Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma at Vikaspuri Police Station.
Saheb Singh stated, 'If any evidence emerges that I used abusive language, I am ready to turn myself in for arrest; I have stated this clearly.'
AAP MLA Jarnail Singh demanded a CBI inquiry into the Tilak Nagar road project and called for Parvesh Verma's immediate suspension.
